fixed.review_text:
No vulnerabilities found in the provided code.

The per-request cap is enforced even when `Content-Length` is missing or understated: the copy is wrapped in `io.LimitReader`, and one extra byte is checked before the digest is returned. Oversized bodies are rejected and the temp file is removed. `os.CreateTemp` is used (exclusive create, `0600`), I/O stays on the open file descriptor, and sync/seek/close failures fail closed without returning a digest.

vuln.review_text:
The code has two security vulnerabilities, both related to how the request body is staged to disk.

**1. body.go:46 — Uncontrolled resource consumption (CWE-770)**
```go
size, err := io.Copy(io.MultiWriter(temporary, digest), request.Body)
```
`io.Copy` reads `request.Body` with no size cap (`http.MaxBytesReader`, `io.LimitReader`, or a checked `ContentLength`). A caller can stream an arbitrarily large body, filling the temp filesystem and tying up the process until the copy fails.

**2. body.go:36 — Sensitive data written to a shared temp directory (CWE-377 / CWE-312)**
```go
temporary, err := os.CreateTemp("", "nginx-ui-node-request-body-*")
```
The full request body is written under `os.TempDir()` and, on the success path (line 65), is left there until something else closes and removes it. A crash or a missed cleanup leaves the body on disk; the `nginx-ui-node-request-body-*` name also makes those files easy to spot.
